Manifesto.label: What is StayLooped?
Manifesto.body: StayLooped is a small, curated guide to Chiang Mai's best-loved tours and activities. We pick a tight shortlist of vetted operators — the ones with consistent reviews and the kind of experience we'd send a friend on.
Manifesto.bodyExtra: Bookings go straight to the operator. We earn a small commission on links you click, at no extra cost to you. That's what keeps this guide free.

Guide.title: A few apps that'll make your Chiang Mai trip a lot easier
Guide.subtitle: We use all of these ourselves — thought they'd be handy to have on your phone before you arrive.
Guide.klookTagline: book experiences and day trips in advance
Guide.klookP1: Most of the tours and activities on this site are bookable through <link>Klook</link>. It's what we'd recommend for anything that needs a time slot — elephant sanctuaries, cooking classes, day trips out of the city.
Guide.klookP2: One thing many guests don't realise: Klook also has private car hire for full-day trips. If you want to do Doi Inthanon, Chiang Rai, or Pai at your own pace with a driver who knows the roads, this is the most comfortable way to do it. You set the itinerary, the driver handles the rest. Search "Chiang Mai private car" on Klook →
Guide.klookP3: The main reason to book ahead: popular experiences sell out, especially on weekends and during high season (November to February). Booking through Klook means instant confirmation, clear pickup details, and a refund policy if plans change.
Guide.lazadaTagline: order souvenirs and essentials to your door
Guide.lazadaP1: <link>Lazada</link> is Thailand's biggest online marketplace — think Amazon, but for Southeast Asia. Prices are often significantly cheaper than tourist-area shops.
Guide.lazadaP2: Our tip: order a few things to the house a day or two after you arrive. Sunscreen, insect repellent, a power adapter, snacks, a daypack — all the things you'd otherwise spend an afternoon hunting for. Delivery to Chiang Mai is usually 1–3 days.
Guide.lazadaTip1: Look for "Lazada Mall" when buying anything branded. Mall sellers are official brand stores — more reliable quality and easier returns.
Guide.lazadaTip2: Always check the reviews before you buy, especially from non-Mall sellers.
Guide.lazadaTip3: Check the shipping date carefully. Some items ship from overseas and can take 1–2 weeks — if you're leaving soon, filter for Thailand sellers only.
Guide.lazadaP3: Also great for Thai souvenirs — textiles, local snacks, handicrafts — order online and have them delivered straight to where you're staying. No haggling, no carrying bags around all day.
Guide.grabP1: <link>Grab</link> is the Uber of Southeast Asia — rides, motorbike taxis, and food delivery in one app. In Chiang Mai it's the most reliable way to get around without negotiating tuk-tuk fares.
Guide.grabP2: Fixed prices shown upfront, no surprises. But beyond the basics: Grab also lets you book a driver for a full day. Tell the driver where you want to go — Doi Suthep, the elephant sanctuary, a temple loop outside the city — agree on a price, and they'll wait for you at each stop. Flexible, personal, and often cheaper than a group tour.
Guide.grabP3: GrabFood is solid for evenings in. Coverage around Chiang Mai is good.
Guide.translateP1: The camera mode is the one to know. Point your phone at a menu, a sign, or a product label and it translates instantly — no typing needed.
Guide.translateP2: Download the Thai language pack before you leave the house so it works offline too. Chinese is usually pre-installed but worth double-checking.
Guide.lineP1: LINE is the messaging app that runs Thailand. Locals, restaurants, tour operators, drivers — everyone's on it. If you're staying for more than a week or planning to come back, it's worth setting up.
Guide.lineP2: Practically: some local restaurants only take bookings via LINE. Small tour operators and private drivers prefer it. A few market vendors use LINE Pay. Think of it less as a chat app and more as the national communication layer.
Guide.closing: You're looped in. With these on your phone, you're already travelling more like a local than most tourists ever will. Go explore like you actually live here.
